conclusions: All four removals lower T and raise departure from DA; depth and edge have the largest effects here.
The relative influence of factors differs from Tokyo; this is descriptive evidence from two clips.
Full E4 and leave-one-out outputs show subtle local changes but no established overall perceptual winner.
E3 shows more mottled/smoothed local train and passenger structure in the inspected early windows.
Retain frozen full E4; report the smoothing tradeoff and limited visual evidence.
limitations: Fixed RGB/flow reference excludes some occlusion and boundary regions.
No depth GT; lower T is not accuracy or perceptual quality.
Departure from DA is not error; DA is not ground truth.
Frame pairs are correlated; no significance test.
Removing a soft term preserves hard gates and optical flow warping.
Historical and new runtime measurements are not a shared benchmark.
Post-hoc study; frozen main result is unchanged.
Decoded still sequences, not real-time playback; diagnostic windows are not random; the fixed crop does not cover every moving object position.
